audit_findings.title: Earnout liability omitted from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $49.962 million recorded at June 28, 2026, equal to approximately $2.38 per diluted share
audit_findings.mechanism: The recorded WaterSurplus and Water Solutions earnout liabilities are claims ahead of common equity and should enter the equity bridge unless their settlements are already charged to forecast OE.
audit_findings.evidence: The maximum earnout liability of $ 53.7 million was discounted and recorded at the estimated present value of $ 43.0 million at the acquisition date.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated bridge omission, not merely a possible exposure. The latest filing records $45.433 million of long-term and $4.529 million of current earnout liabilities. Deducting $49.962 million would reduce base equity value from $1.525 billion to about $1.475 billion and base value per share from $72.65 to about $70.27. Although it would not reverse the present overvaluation versus the $129.13 market price, the known claim is large enough to require correction of the valuation outputs.
audit_findings.action: Confirm that no earnout settlement is included in forecast OE, then rerun every scenario and the buy-below price with the June 28, 2026 recorded liability deducted from the bridge.

audit_findings.title: Growth may depend on acquisition spending excluded from owner earnings
audit_findings.mechanism: Recurring acquisition cash requirements would reduce distributable OE or require lower organic growth assumptions; excluding them can overstate both forecast growth and the cash available to owners.
audit_findings.evidence: In fiscal 2026, we incurred acquisition spending of $167.1 million, including the acquisition of WaterSurplus for $149.9 million paid at closing, compared to $87.4 million of acquisition spending in fiscal 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The concern is reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion. Hawkins spent $167.1 million on acquisitions in fiscal 2026 and $87.4 million in fiscal 2025. Acquired businesses contributed $83.3 million of the $109.3 million fiscal-2026 sales increase and $72.1 million against a $55.2 million consolidated increase in fiscal 2025. The record therefore demonstrates substantial acquisition dependence in historical reported growth, but it does not quantify acquired versus organic OE or the spending required to sustain the forecast. Moving from the 5%-8% cases toward the 0% case spans $17.48-$30.40 per share, so resolving the issue could materially alter scenario value.
audit_findings.action: Build organic and acquired revenue, operating profit, and OE bridges by acquisition cohort; identify acquisition cash needed to support each forecast growth rate; then rerun growth and OE after charging any recurring acquisition requirement.

audit_findings.title: A nonrecurring earnout gain may remain in anchor earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $6.177 million net pretax earnout gain in fiscal 2026, approximately $4.61 million after the filed 25.4% tax rate if retained
audit_findings.mechanism: A retained noncash earnout remeasurement gain would inflate the $96.7 million OE anchor and all forecast OE, including terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: This was partially offset by a reduction of $8.1 million to the Water Solutions earnout.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates a nonrecurring $8.075 million Water Solutions liability reduction, partly offset by a $1.898 million WaterSurplus increase, producing a net $6.177 million pretax gain. The record supplied does not show the detailed OE reconciliation, so it cannot establish whether the gain survived the cash-flow and normalization adjustments. If fully retained after tax, it would be about 4.8% of the anchor and would imply roughly $72 million, or $3.44 per share, of base-case value under the existing model. Materiality therefore remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Trace the fiscal-2026 OE calculation line by line through net income and cash-flow adjustments; confirm removal of both earnout remeasurements and rerun from a normalized anchor if any net gain remains.

audit_findings.title: Unpaid environmental remediation is absent from the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $7.7 million filed liability, approximately $0.37 per diluted share and 0.50% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Because the expense was recognized before the anchor year while the cash remains payable, the liability should reduce the equity bridge or be charged as a future OE cash outflow.
audit_findings.evidence: The remediation liability is not discounted as management expects to incur these expenses within the next twelve months.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated omission: the June 28, 2026 balance sheet still reports the full $7.7 million current liability. Its scale is only about 0.50% of the $1.525 billion base equity value and would reduce base value by approximately $0.37 per share, leaving the valuation conclusion unchanged. Additional remediation is only reasonably possible and remains unquantified.
audit_findings.action: Deduct the recorded $7.7 million from the bridge or explicitly schedule its payment outside recurring OE; separately monitor filings for any increase beyond the recorded amount.

audit_findings.title: Potential facility-removal obligations are unrecorded
audit_findings.mechanism: If a lease is not renewed and the lessor requires removal, relocation or demolition cash costs would reduce future OE or require a liability deduction.
audit_findings.evidence: Therefore, in accordance with accounting guidance related to asset retirement and environmental obligations, we have not recorded an asset retirement obligation as of March 29, 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a forward-looking contingent exposure rather than a demonstrated present valuation error. The company could not reasonably estimate a liability, has historically extended the leases, intends to renew them, and believes the buildings may retain value. Nevertheless, the earliest lease expires in 2029 within the explicit forecast period, so the renewal and removal assumptions require monitoring.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the 2029 lease terms, renewal negotiations, site-specific removal estimates, relocation costs, and lessor intentions; probability-weight the cash costs if nonrenewal becomes more than remote.

audit_findings.title: Legacy pension withdrawal payments are an unbridged claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $3.504 million filed undiscounted contractual payments at March 29, 2026; latest long-term liability was $2.663 million, with the $3.504 million schedule equal to approximately $0.17 per diluted share and 0.23% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Payments through 2034 reduce equity cash after the associated expense was recognized in 2013, so the remaining obligation belongs in the bridge unless forecast OE includes the payments.
audit_findings.evidence: Payments of approximately $ 0.5 million per year are being made through 2034.
audit_findings.explanation: The unbridged claim is demonstrated, but its scale is not material to the conclusion. Even using the filed $3.504 million undiscounted payment schedule rather than the smaller recorded long-term balance, the effect is only about 0.23% of base equity value and $0.17 per share.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the June 28, 2026 current and long-term portions, then deduct the remaining present-value liability from the bridge or document that all scheduled payments are included in forecast OE.
